headline: US New Home Sales Jump 14.2% in October to Seasonally Adjusted 701,000
summary: Sales of new single-family homes in the United States surged 14.2% in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 701,000 units, beating market forecasts.
why: Housing market indicators reflect consumer demand, borrowing costs, and broader economic momentum in the domestic real estate sector.

impacts.name: United States
impacts.why: An increase in new home sales indicates stronger real estate demand.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: A stronger-than-expected jump in new home sales signaled resilient consumer demand in the housing sector despite elevated interest rates.
